title: Traditional games of the Karbi people
description: Dharamsing Teron talks about his childhood in the 1960s and how the Karbi people lived then. He describes two games: walking on stilts so that thorns don't pierce bare feet on swampy ground, and Hambi (IPA /haːmbi/), played with locally grown nickernuts. In Hambi, two teams with the same number of players, at least two each, stand about five metres apart. The game has stages, each with its own name, and the players tease the other team. Subhashish Panigrahi interviewed him remotely, with his permission, on 21 May 2017. This is part 4 of the nine-part interview, and mjw010 is the full recording.
